reinforcement_note: Mechanical sweep of readmodel/standards_spine.json on 2026-10-28: no skill has n=0, so no uncovered skill exists. Thinnest forced skills (n<=3) are claimed as reinforcement: combination how-to (n=2), binomial coefficient term and how-to (n=2), factorial term and how-to (n=3), combination term (n=4). Adjacent skills considered and NOT claimed: independent-event (n=2; hypergeometric draws are dependent, claiming it would be wrong), dependent-event (counting method handles it; no deliverable performs a dependent-event calculation), permutation how-to (n=2; order never matters here), compound-event probability (n=7; the window is a sum of counts, not a compound-event calculation), conditional probability (n=5; only the Twist's redraw touches it and that is facilitator-only). The binomial/factorial claims are forced only by D1, which forbids a table or combinations key and requires factorial cancellation; Appendix C gives the definition of C(n,k), not any value.

appendices.title: The Windows To Test, And The Margin Convention

balance.argument_a: The Sixteen-Land List leads on the draw (0.8522 against 0.8470, 0.61%), in 3 of 9 windows in Appendix D (2-5 by 5.84%, 2-6 by 1.75%, 3-5 by 3.40%), and through turn 5 (2.13%). It carries one more spell in every hand (expected spells among the first 11 cards 6.600 against 6.325) and, after a free redraw of 0/1/6/7-land hands, it leads the primary metric 0.8998 to 0.8949.
balance.argument_b: The Seventeen-Land List leads on the play (0.8550 against 0.8370, 2.10%), in 6 of 9 windows (largest 4-7 by 7.72%), through turn 3 (3.27%), and on the no-play hand: 10.52% against 13.41%, 21.54% fewer. Its averaged probability of a smooth start is 0.8510 against 0.8446, and 17 is the peak of the averaged curve over 14 to 19 lands.
balance.margin_basis: Primary: (0.8510 - 0.8446)/0.8510 = 0.75%, gap divided by the winner's value, 3-to-6 window, turn 4, 50/50 play/draw. The margin is window-driven (0.14% to 7.72% pooled across the Appendix D grid). Secondary (no-play hand, lower better) 21.54% for B.
balance.twist_effect: A free one-time redraw of an opening 7 with 0, 1, 6 or 7 lands moves the primary lead to Option A (0.8998 against 0.8949, 0.54%). It invalidates 'B is better because it avoids the no-land hand' without making A obviously right; with redraw only on 0/1 A still leads (0.99%), with redraw also on 2 lands the two tie (0.07%).

cohort_bands.note: Socratic plan runs as written. Real show-of-hands at Anchor 1; both threads run. Split the window grid across pairs, then compare.

Combine Anchors 2 and 3 into one pass. Run only Thread 1 (what counts as a good start). Twist still drops at 15:00. About 30 minutes. Pre-fill the D3 distribution as a spreadsheet so the grid is a sum.

No vote at Anchor 1: the learner states an initial position. The guide argues the other side directly. The twist still lands; 'who reverses' becomes 'would you reverse, and why'. Skip the threads and go from twist-recommit to Close.

sensitivity_disclosure.justification: MA2 fixes the window's lower bound at 3 before calculation. Flexed to 2 (from 1.5) A leads 1.75%; to 4 (from 4.5) B leads 5.78%. The verdict is not stable to the window and the case says so (Appendix D, D4, D6).
Upper bound 3 to 9 from 6: at 3 (exactly three lands) A leads by 16.20%, inside the 20% cap; at 9 B leads by 3.25%.
Horizon 2 to 6 from 4: through turn 2 B leads 5.51%, through turn 6 A leads 5.33%; through turn 3 B 3.27%, turn 5 A 2.13%.
0.25 gives B by 0.07%, 0.75 gives B by 1.43%; A leads only when the play share is below about 22.5%. The verdict is stable to this dial in the flex range.
